title: introduce-cross-cohort-surge-fingerprinter-and-throttle-orchestrator
author: Samira Patel
description:
Context: Global canary signals routinely miss short-lived, cohort-specific surges that cause tail latency regressions for a subset of traffic (e.g. tenants, regions, or new client SDK versions). These transient bursts can evade aggregate detectors and lead to customer-facing regressions during staged rollouts.

Motivation: We need a lightweight detector that attributes short-lived latency shifts to traffic cohorts, correlates surge fingerprints with tail-percentile shifts, and enforces a conservative throttle/rollback budget so rollouts stay safe without over-triggering on noisy signals.

What this PR does: Adds a cross-cohort surge fingerprinter plus a throttle orchestrator that integrates into the existing canary pipeline. The fingerprinter builds a compact, time-windowed sketch for each cohort (traffic key) and produces a normalized "surge signature" vector. The orchestrator computes similarity between new and baseline signatures, correlates with percentile shifts (p50/p95/p99), and applies an adaptive probe-throttle or rollback-credit policy. The feature is behind the existing canary feature-flag and defaults to off for user-triggered rollouts.

Implementation notes: - Cross-cohort fingerprinter implemented in perf-canary/detectors/fingerprinter.go using a sliding window Count-Min + truncated histogram sketch to keep memory bounded. - Surge similarity uses cosine distance with decay-weighted recent windows to prefer sustained divergence. - Orchestrator (perf-canary/orchestrator/throttle_orchestrator.py) exposes three policy knobs: sensitivity, stability-window, and rollback-credit-rate. - Metrics: new labels/metrics prefixed with pc_cohort_ (pc_cohort_surge_score, pc_cohort_similarity, pc_cohort_throttle_actions). - Integrations: hooks added to canary-evaluator to provide cohort-aware gating and to the rollout controller to consume throttle decisions.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for fingerprinter accuracy and memory bound checks. - Integration tests using the synthetic-traffic-replay harness to simulate skewed cohort bursts and verify correct gating. - Benchmarks: microbenchmark shows ~1.8% median CPU increase and <4ms p99 additional latency on the detector path for typical traffic shapes; acceptable for Dedicated and Hosted with feature-flag toggled.

Checklist: [x] Design doc linked (ENG-2145) [x] Unit tests [x] Integration e2e test in perf lab [x] Metrics + dashboards updated [x] Feature-flag gating [x] Backwards-compatible changes only

Backward compatibility / migration: All changes are behind a feature flag. Fingerprinter state stored in ephemeral in-memory stores with an optional Redis-backed persistence (opt-in in config). No schema migrations.

Risks and mitigations: Memory growth for extreme cardinality cohorts mitigated by per-customer caps and a global eviction policy. False positives reduced by requiring both surge similarity and percentile correlation before throttle/rollback credit application.

Related: ENG-2145 (design), ENG-2199 (test harness), SUP-4123 (customer incident that motivated this work).

review_comments: Evan Brooks: Can you quantify max memory per 10k cohorts? Request adding a forced-eviction unit test.
Samira Patel (author): Per 10k cohorts we cap to 8MB total with the truncated histogram; added eviction test and doc comments.
Maya Chen: Important to ensure the similarity metric isn't sensitive to benign distribution shifts (e.g., seasonal). Please add a decay window config and a short rationale.
Samira Patel (author): Added stability-window config and updated docs to explain decay rationale (see docs/designs/cross_cohort_fingerprinter.md).
Oliver Kim: CI showed intermittent failure on bench harness; looks like noise in synthetic replay. Please add retry and increase seed determinism.
Samira Patel (author): Increased determinism in the harness and added retry logic. Re-ran bench and updated reported numbers in PR description.
Evan Brooks: Approving pending small nits in metric naming (prefer pc_cohort_surge_score over pc_cohort_surge).
Samira Patel (author): Renamed metrics accordingly and updated dashboards.
Maya Chen: Approved. Suggest rolling out to canary-1 first with throttle sensitivity=0.7 and rollback-credit-rate=0.1.

release_notes: Add cohort-aware surge detection and adaptive throttle orchestrator: introduces pc_cohort_surge_score and pc_cohort_similarity metrics; defaults off behind feature-flag; rollout recommended start with canary-1 and conservative knobs
